runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: Prescott yard arrive in good form (5 from 24 over 14 days), this 4yo has back-to-back placed efforts at 10f on Good and a win at 10f on Good, stepping up to 12f today is the main query but the draw in 12 is fine for a midfield tracker.
runners_data.comment: Almekarem has placed in back-to-back runs and a win four starts back gives him a decent recent profile, though a seventh three starts back is the blot; he has run over today's trip and going, returns fit on 11 days, and a yard firing at 26% gives him every chance from stall 12 off 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Newtown Duke
runners_data.note: 90-day absence is a concern for this hold-up performer, though he won at 8f on Firm and placed at 12f on Good and Soft — Ian Williams runners can arrive fit fresh but the layoff combined with only one placed at 12f on similar ground tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Newtown Duke has reasonable claims on form but his trainer's poor recent strike-rate and a 90-day absence are real concerns; he has run over today's trip and going, which at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Reveur
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity: lightly raced 3yo with 126-day absence, style unclassified and form figures showing a zero make this a genuine puzzle — David O'Meara's record over 14 days is solid (5 from 56) but Tudhope takes the ride suggesting connections are interested, yet insufficient data to profile confidently.
runners_data.comment: Reveur showed he has the ability to win when successful four starts back, and with a lengthy absence of 126 days now behind him, he arrives relatively unexposed and open to further progress carrying 132 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: Strand scorecard danger; Jessica Macey's yard is cold (0 from 10 over 14 days) but this 4yo is in excellent form with four placings in his last five including a win at 10f on Good — Sean Levey is a meaningful booking and the prominent style suits a strongly-run 10f-equivalent test perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Everyoneknowsadave filled the runner-up spot last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but he was fourth two starts back and has managed only one win in his last six starts, making him a tough nut to crack from stall 6 off 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Director's Cut
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who showed a win at 8f on Firm and has placed twice at 10f+ on Good, but his last five include two blanks at 12f and zero places on Good over the trip — wearing a hood (hg:p) and 74 days fresh, he will go forward but the step to 12f turf in a hot pace battle is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well held on our figures in a 19-runner field, Director's Cut arrives unplaced last time out and has mustered only one win in his last five starts, making him hard to fancy. He has run over today's trip before and 131 lb is workable, but the case for him is slim.

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos
runners_data.note: Hold-up 4yo who placed at 10f on Good twice in recent form and won at 10f on Firm, returning just 8 days after his last run which could mean the stable are bullish — Rowan Scott's booking is notable and stamina to 12f looks plausible given pedigree, though he has never started at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Ranked a long way down the field on our figures and drawn in stall ten, Amidst The Chaos faces a stiff ask, with his trainer returning just one winner from twenty-two runners in the last fortnight; he has run over today's trip and returns on a quick turnaround, but that is modest consolation.

runners_data.name: Without Compromise
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's 5yo tracked prominently at 10f on Good for a runner-up last time (2 from 10 on sim-going) and is well in at OR-79 given recent form — Cam Hardie rides and the step to 12f suits a horse who stays, though he has no confirmed 12f form and the early prominent berth may be harder to find in a 19-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Without Compromise has shown he can mix it at this level — a second two starts back offers encouragement — but a sixth last time out and winless in his last five starts give pause; has run over today's trip and arrives on a handy 26-day break, though his rating of 78 leaves him mid-pack in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: Tina Jackson's 5yo has two second-place finishes in last five at 8-10f on Good and Good-to-Soft — Joanna Mason keeps the ride, the draw in 14 is neutral but the horse is running prominently off the pace and the lack of 12f form is the key unknown here.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, His Finest Hour at least brings strong place consistency — second and third among those efforts — and has run over today's trip and going before; 133 lb from stall 14 is the counterweight, though a return to form isn't out of the question.

runners_data.name: Optician
runners_data.note: Strand scorecard danger; Conor Whiteley (5lb claimer) rides this Michael Herrington 6yo who WON at 12f on Soft and placed at 10f on Good — midfield style suits this shape well, though nine recent outings without a win and inconsistent form (9th and 10th in last two starts) are genuine negatives to weigh.
runners_data.comment: Optician showed he can win in recent starts, with a second two starts back adding further encouragement, but a ninth last time out clouds his claims; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 136 lb from stall 16 after a 25-day absence.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner but warned for fading in finishes — Scott Dixon's 4yo has never finished better than second and that was at 8f on Soft, his Good-ground form over 8f is poor (finishes 6th, 9th, 14th) and the step to 12f makes him a sacrifice pacemaker rather than a genuine contender.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Canvas nonetheless catches the eye on profile, stepping back up to familiar distance and going conditions, and he arrives fit on just a five-day turnaround; second last time out lifts the spirits, though the trainer's current run of form is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: Strand scorecard top selection; David Egan takes the mount for Gemma Tutty, this 3yo won at 8f on Good and has been placed once more — the hold-up style is suited by the hot pace and Doncaster's straight run-in, though the 19 draw is wide and the step to 12f from 8f is a significant trip hike needing stamina to be confirmed.
runners_data.comment: Illy's Roo was a winner four starts back but has disappointed in his last three outings, including a ninth last time out just five days ago, leaving his form under a cloud; he has run over today's going before and a mark of 77 gives him something to work with.

runners_data.name: On The Inlet
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo who won twice over 7f including on Firm, placed three from eight on Good ground — confirmed front-runner drawn 13 and will be competitive early, but form has tailed off since leaving shorter trips (3-3-5-3 in last four) and the 12f distance appears beyond his optimum.
runners_data.comment: On The Inlet brings solid recent form — third last time out and third two starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, with a rating of 82 supporting his claims; however, he carries 132 lb from stall 13 and has been out of the placings in two of his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's 5yo won over 9f on Soft and 17f on Soft showing extreme stamina versatility, 75-day break is the key risk — prominent style with good 12f form (placed at 12f on Good) and Tom Eaves is a positive booking, but no trainer 14-day strike rate warmth (2 from 11) tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Amancio franked his recent form with a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and the going, with his official mark of 79 looking workable off stall four; the main concern is the 75-day absence since that victory.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with three wins over 8f on Good including a track win, but all his success is at 8-9f and this step to 12f on a flat, stamina-testing track against rivals who outstay him is problematic — the pace role he plays will likely benefit others more than himself.
runners_data.comment: Highland Olly has struggled for consistency in recent starts, finishing seventh and fifth in his last two before rallying to third last time out, and his rating of 75 ranks him fourteenth of nineteen here, making him difficult to fancy despite having run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Naples
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes this Steph Hollinshead 4yo who has produced a single third from 12f on Soft, finishing 12th and 12th elsewhere at the trip — hold-up style and wearing a hood (hg:p), but the consistent mediocrity (5th, 0th, 0th, 3rd, 5th in last five) makes this a speculative inclusion.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and winless in recent starts, Naples brings distance-and-going experience and a lively fitness edge at 26 days since his last run, with his third three starts back offering a form pointer — though he must convert that promise under 134 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's presence on Hugo Palmer's 3yo commands attention — three wins from nine at 9-10f on Soft, placed once at 12f on Firm, and the hood (hg:p) suggests headgear aids focus; the hold-up style suits the shape but all winning form is on Soft and the Good ground is a minor query.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures and drawn in stall 17, Fans Favourite is hard to fancy despite a lively recent record that includes wins in his last six starts, most recently a winner thirteen days ago, and experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Something Splendid
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes Peter Chapple-Hyam's 4yo who won at 10f on Soft last time from a 0-4-9-7 sequence — prominent style drawn widish in 2 and the win was on Soft, with Good-ground form uninspiring (7th, 9th, 11th); the class angle is there but consistency has been elusive.
runners_data.comment: Something Splendid won last time out but that sits alongside three poor efforts in his last four starts before it, and ranked 13 of 19 on our figures he faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going and returns on a fresh enough 12-day break.

runners_data.name: Spirit Genie
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's 6yo won at 8f on Good most recently from draw 3 — hold-up style with blinkers and a tongue-tie (hg:tb), Jason Hart rides and the course trip upgrade to 12f is the main step, but Good-ground form is strong (win plus a placed effort) and the style suits this shape if stamina proves adequate.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Genie arrives on the back of a win, handles today's distance and going, and a rating of 85 has him firmly in contention from stall three; the main concern is that unplaced run sandwiched between his recent efforts, hinting at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's second runner is a confirmed front-runner who won at 10f on Good last time — 3yo drawn 18, which is wide for early position, and her form at 10f+ on Good is limited; likely to make the running alongside Highland Olly and Canvas and set up the race for others.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Ziata faces a stiff task, and a sixth and an unplaced run in her last two starts do little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a win three starts back shows she can find the line.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly, On The Inlet, Director's Cut, Canvas, and Ziata all carry genuine front-running intent in a field of 19, meaning the early gallop on Doncaster's straight mile-and-a-quarter will be genuinely contested and the pace almost certain to be strong. The leaders will burn each other off through the first half-mile, with the prominent types Everyoneknowsadave, Without Compromise, and Amancio likely tracking the action but unable to dictate — they will be passengers on a hot tempo rather than influential setters. At Doncaster's long run-in, a true-run gallop on Good ground over 1m2f classically sets up the hold-up or deep-midfield horses who can cruise into a strong pace without expending energy early, travel sweetly, then pounce from two out. The tactical verdict is clear: hold-up and midfield runners who possess stamina and can deliver a sustained finish suit this race shape most — deep closers arrive with energy intact while the front end is spent.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If the five-horse pace battle burns out the leaders inside the final quarter-mile, leaving the hold-up runners with a clear run on the long Doncaster straight.
scenarios.body: A genuine hot pace drains the front-runners by the two-furlong pole, and horses that have settled mid-to-rear can sweep past tired rivals with their finishing kicks intact on the flat, forgiving Good ground. The long straight at Doncaster rewards sustained galloping finishes rather than sharp acceleration, making this the highest-probability shape given the preponderance of front-running types.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the tracking prominent types settles just behind the leaders, avoids the war up front, and kicks clear entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Everyoneknowsadave is the primary beneficiary here: OR-75, prominently raced, with four placed efforts in ten Good-ground outings and genuine tactical versatility at 10-11f — they can stalk and pounce if the pace is honest enough to weaken those ahead. Without Compromise and Almekarem could also capitalise if they find clear daylight early in the straight rather than getting boxed behind the midfield cluster.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leaders Steal It Soft
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves more moderate than expected despite the numbers, allowing one front-runner to conserve energy and hold on through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With five putative leaders, one scenario is that the rest panic-check each other and a canny operator slips the field at a controlled clip — Director's Cut showed a course-and-distance win at 8f in soft conditions and might find company thinning out quickly if rivals eye each other. Highland Olly has front-running track record on Good ground, but the more likely beneficiary of a relatively uncontested lead is whichever of the pace brigade has the sharpest handler on the day.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Grind Suits Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so relentlessly strong that the race becomes a stamina test throughout, with the winner grinding out the final furlong rather than quickening.
scenarios.body: Horses with proven form at 12f or beyond come into their own here — Optician won over 12f in soft and placed over 10f on Good, while Amancio has run well over marathon trips and could strip fitter for a 75-day break if the yard is ready. This outcome requires the deepest closers and most resolute stayers to prevail, and the relatively few confirmed 12f performers in this field limit the probability.

watchPoints.text: Watch the pace war between Highland Olly, On The Inlet, Director's Cut, Canvas, and Ziata — if all five go hard from the off, the leaders could be cooked by halfway, and any hold-up horse (Illy's Roo, Amidst The Chaos, Spirit Genie) that tracks the chaos without getting involved early becomes dangerous from two out.

Oisin Murphy's booking on Fans Favourite (Hugo Palmer, 3yo, hat-trick seeker) is above the horse's market price — watch whether the yard has flagged this as a readiness run or a live chance, as Murphy rarely rides without purpose in a competitive handicap.
